parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: That's fine, let's make it smaller. What was the very first thing you did when you got to work this morning?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: No problem. Think of the last drone you had your hands on: what were you doing with it?

Q4
The answer just before it: I was keeping the drone in working order by adding a new one to the fleet, retiring an old one, taking it out of service for repairs and putting it back, or sending it to charge. My company runs a few hundred drones of several models from different manufacturers, which differ in their carrying capacity, flight range on a full battery, sensors, and charging connectors.
The question: Tell me about the last time you took one specific drone out of service for repair. What happened, step by step?

Q5
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You mentioned that the models differ in capacity, range, sensors, and charging connectors. When do those differences matter in your own work?

Q6
The answer just before it: I need to know those differences because we run a few hundred drones of several models from different manufacturers, and their charging connectors are not interchangeable. That matters when I set up charging pads at our sites or when I send drones to charge.
The question: Tell me more about setting up charging pads at your sites. What does that involve?

Q7
The answer just before it: I set up charging pads at our sites, and we have a few dozen of them. This is part of keeping our equipment in working order, alongside my work with the drones.
The question: When you send a drone to charge, how do you decide which pad it goes to?

Q8
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Let's move to something different. Think of the worst day you've had at work in the last few months. What happened?

Q9
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Has anything ever gone wrong with a drone or a charging pad that you had to deal with? Tell me about one such case.

Q10
The answer just before it: I keep drones and charging equipment in working order by adding new drones to the fleet, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back, and sending drones to charge. Regulators can ask my company to show how its drones have been looked after.
The question: You said regulators can ask your company to show how its drones have been looked after. What exactly do they ask to see?

Q11
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you finish working on a drone, what do you record about it, and where?

Q12
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you add a new drone to the fleet, what do you have to do before it can fly its first job?

Q13
The answer just before it: I add new drones to the fleet as part of keeping the drones and charging equipment in working order. Beyond that, I don't know what I have to do before it can fly its first job.
The question: Who tells you that a drone needs your attention, and how does that reach you?

Q14
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you put a drone back into service after a repair, who needs to know about it?

Q15
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Is there anything in your work today that you double-check by hand because you don't trust what you've been told or shown?

Q16
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: If a new service were brought in for your work tomorrow, what would worry you most about it?

Q17
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Imagine a drone has just failed in some way. What is the first thing you would want to find out?

Q18
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What do you use today to keep track of a few hundred drones and a few dozen sites?

Q19
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: How do you decide that an old drone should be retired?

Q20
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What do other people in your company need from you in order to do their own work?

Q21
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Who outside your own company, if anyone, should be able to see information about your drones and charging pads?

Q22
The answer just before it: Regulators can ask my company to show how its drones have been looked after. I don't know who else outside my company should be able to see information about our drones and charging pads.
The question: When you take a drone out of service for repair, what happens to the work that drone was supposed to do?

Q23
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You said the charging connectors are not interchangeable. What happens when a drone arrives at a pad with the wrong connector?

Q24

The question: Is there anything about your work that I haven't asked about and that you think I should know?
